title: CmdPal: Gallery refresh loses track of running extensions (EXT26.E1)

judgment.rationale: An isolated test reproduced zero stop calls to the old running wrapper after refresh. Related issue 48433 is closed but concerns installation detection, not running-wrapper lifetime.
evidence: The report reproduces gallery refresh followed by zero stop calls to the old running wrapper.
The described path rebuilds registry wrappers while command providers still hold old references.
Related issue 48433's body concerns installed/not-installed status, not stop delivery.

confidence.rationale: The missed stop call is reproduced; wrapper reuse and retirement across replacements need coverage.

verification: Start an extension, refresh status for an unchanged registration, request stop and verify the original running wrapper is signaled.
Replace/remove a registration and verify its old wrapper is retired while distinct registrations remain separate.
Run gallery refresh and service lifecycle tests.
plan: Reuse wrappers when package version and app-extension/CLSID identity are unchanged.
Retire removed/replaced wrappers explicitly and keep distinct registrations separate.
Track all still-running instances for shutdown, including retired wrappers, without changing enable/disable choices.
Test refresh while an extension is running and verify stop and later reload.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A gallery status refresh rebuilds wrappers for unchanged registrations; running providers retain old instances, but SignalStopAsync walks only the new registry.
proposed_fixes.title: Investigate the reported PowerToys behavior

issue_context.summary: Gallery refresh replaces wrappers for unchanged registrations while running providers retain old wrappers, so stop traversal can miss those live instances.
